gloss: well-bred; well-raised; from a good family

definitions.gloss: well-bred; well-raised; from a good upbringing
definitions.explanation: Describes someone whose manners, behavior, and character reflect a good upbringing and family background. Implies refinement, politeness, and good values instilled during childhood.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{育|そだ}ちが{良|い}い。
{言葉遣|ことばづか}いが{丁寧|ていねい}で、{育|そだ}ちの{良|よ}さがうかがえる。
examples.english: Their polite way of speaking suggests they were well-raised.

examples.japanese: {育|そだ}ちが{良|い}い{人|ひと}は、{食事|しょくじ}のマナーや{人|ひと}への{接|せっ}し{方|かた}に{自然|しぜん}と{品|ひん}が{出|で}るものだ。
examples.english: People who are well-raised naturally show refinement in their table manners and how they treat others.

notes:
USAGE:
The opposite expression is {育|そだ}ちが{悪|わる}い (poorly raised). This expression is commonly used when commenting on someone's manners or background, but should be used carefully as it can sound judgmental. The い-adjective form {良|い}い is more common in speech than {良|よ}い.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {育|そだ}ちの{良|よ}さ (the quality of one's upbringing)
- {育|そだ}ちが{良|い}い{人|ひと} (a well-bred person)
- {育|そだ}ちの{良|よ}い{家庭|かてい} (a well-brought-up family)
